candidates.text:
Of course, that’s your contention. You’re a first-year machine-learning engineer. You just got finished readin' Attention Is All You Need, probably watched a Karpathy video too. So now you’re convinced everything is just transformers and scaling laws.

That's gonna last until next month when you discover convolution, and then you're gonna be talkin' about inductive biases and locality and how CNNs were actually incredibly compute-efficient for vision.

Then you're gonna read the FlashAttention paper, and suddenly everything's about IO complexity and SRAM and how FLOPs don't matter because the whole goddamn thing is memory-bandwidth bound.

That'll last until somebody shows you an MoE model, and then you're gonna be in here regurgitating DeepSeek, talkin' about expert parallelism and active parameters and how dense models are economically obsolete.

Then six months from now you'll write one shitty Triton kernel, look at an Nsight trace for the first time, and start telling everybody Python isn't actually the bottleneck because the GPU is asynchronous.

And by next year you're gonna be standing right here explaining to me that your 400-billion-parameter model is fast because you turned on CUDA graphs.

Why Most Creators and Artists Are Left Wing

People who create right wing content learn very quickly that it is very difficult to earn any money from a right wing audience.

Right wing people are overall extremely stingy with their money regardless of whether they are rich or middle class or poor. They have a scarcity mindset where they only spend money if they are *sure* of profiting off it.

Right wing people EXPECT creators to promote what they believe is “truth” but they themselves act like creators have secretly discovered alchemy and are able to convert rocks to gold to be able to pay the bills.

The reality is that most creators also have to pay rent, want to go out to eat once in a while, have to pay for a family, have children’s expenses, etc. and DO NOT have a magic ability to turn inferior metals into gold.

When the rubber meets the road, right wing creators realize that they are MUCH better off being left wing.

Left wing audiences spend money to attain cultural dominance and find ways to reward those who support them. It is MUCH easier for left wing creators to get brand deals, sponsors, donations, ad revenue, and other income than it is for right wing creators.

The left wing has spent a long time building an entire ecosystem that ensures that creators/artists/famous people who support them get paid.

So if you’re popular and left wing, you WILL be reached out to by brands, be offered sponsorship deals, speaking gigs, be given awards to help you build your brand, etc. This is not by accident.

This is a well coordinated system that strongly incentivizes creators to support the left wing.

The right wing on the other hand is too stupid and too stingy to build financial incentives for creators.

Stingy because they do not want to spend any money unless they see a direct and proven ROI from the spend.

Stupid because they do not understand the value of dominating culture. There is a reason why publicly expressing right wing opinions gets you blackballed in most places, and publicly expressing left wing opinions makes you seem sophisticated.

Running email for 250+ ecom brands taught me that subscriber churn is almost never a pricing problem

When a customer cancels their subscription on month two, it is usually because they lost product usage momentum or forgot why they bought

Most brands try to fix this churn by throwing a 20% discount at the cancellation flow

What actually works is building automated post purchase education sequences that walk the customer through getting real results in their first thirty days

If you teach buyers how to get value out of your product immediately, retention handles itself

What happens when your home appliances can talk to an AI agent? We just found out

Today we're launching the Atomberg MCP Server, built on top of our public APIs.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is quickly becoming the standard way for AI tools to connect to the real world. With our server, any MCP-compatible AI tool can now discover and control Atomberg devices directly. No custom integrations and no glue code

What's in this release:

Natural-language control of Atomberg smart fans
Public API support for water purifiers, newly added
Public API support for smart locks, newly added

These additions came straight from developer requests, and we're glad to finally ship them.

But the part we are most excited about is what we didn't build. Pair an AI agent with your calendar, weather data, or your own scripts, and the possible use cases go well beyond a remote control

If you build something with it, tag us. We would love to see it

For several months now, my household has been in the throes of a raging debate: the pronunciation of "homogeneous". Do we call it homo-JEE-nius or huh-MAW-genus?

Evidence has been presented and discarded; examples have been sought from increasingly obscure sources; appeals have been made to authority; the internet has been deemed unreliable and dusty dictionaries cracked open.

Yet neither side has given an inch. At this point the household is divided into two religious factions locked into a perpetual holy war. The goal is no longer to convince the other side of the supreme truth - it is to overwhelm them with numbers till they're forced to convert. With an innocent-sounding question, very visitor is forced to pick a side; victory is declared after every departure, but defeat never conceded.

With this background, i invite all of twitter to weigh in. Let us show the other side that right prevails over wrong no matter the odds. Satyamev Jayate.

Most brand owners are good at paid ads and front-end marketing

The reason they fail is because of their systems

Pouring thousands of dollars of ad spend into a leaky retention system with bad messaging just burns your profit margin faster than you can scale

The 4 backend systems you need to plug the leak:

- Flow congruence: match your post-purchase copy directly to the creative hook and problem that convinced them to buy on Meta
- Habit building: eliminate buyer's remorse by mapping out a Day 1 to Day 30 benefits timeline before their package lands
- Consumption replenishment: trigger reorder prompts right before their supply runs out based on actual daily usage
- Billing friction: send an alert 48 hours before recurring charges with 1-click pause or flavor swap options so they never hit cancel

Audit your retention flows this week and plug the leaks before pouring more budget into Meta
